files.name: FileController.java

notes.4: Handler taking a `name` request parameter — attacker-controlled.
notes.5: The directory files are supposed to come from.
notes.6: Resolves `name` against the base directory to form the target path.
notes.7: Reads the entire file at that path.
notes.8: Returns its bytes to the client.

options.label: `base.resolve(name)` with `../` segments — or an absolute `name`, which replaces the base entirely — produces a path outside `base`, which is then read
`readAllBytes` loads the whole file into memory, risking exhaustion
options.whyWrong: A large-file DoS is a different concern; the flaw is reading a file outside the intended directory.

options.label: `@RequestParam` without `required=false` throws when absent
options.whyWrong: Parameter presence is unrelated to the traversal.

options.label: Reject name if it contains '..'
options.diff:
+    if (name.contains("..")) throw new AccessDeniedException(name);
     Path target = base.resolve(name);
options.whyWrong: Misses absolute paths and encoded forms; blocklisting is fragile.

options.label: Normalize the resolved path and confirm it stays under base
Catch IOException and return 404
options.whyWrong: Error handling doesn't confine the path; an existing file outside base is still served.

training.exploit: Request `?name=../../../../etc/passwd` to climb out of `/var/data/files`, or `?name=/etc/passwd` — Java's `resolve` of an absolute path discards the base. Either reads an arbitrary file.

hints.line: Where does user input join a filesystem path?
hints.bugClass: Input steers which path is read.
hints.why: What does resolve() do with `..` or an absolute path?
hints.fix: Normalize and verify the result is still under base.

writeup.summary: `base.resolve(name)` trusts `name`: `../` segments climb out of the base directory, and an absolute `name` makes `resolve` return that absolute path outright, discarding the base. `readAllBytes` then returns any file the process can read. The fix normalizes the resolved path and checks `startsWith(base)` before reading, so anything that escapes is rejected.
